title: Electronic Reconstruction Towards Topological Superconductivity in FeTe
authors: Hongtao Rong, Yang Ge, Zi-Jie Yan, Haoran Lin, Bing Xia, Xiaoda Liu, Zihao Wang, Pu Xiao, Lok-Kan Lai, Stephen Paplini, Jiatao Song, Jiangang Yang, Peter J. Hirschfeld, Shuolong Yang, Jiabin Yu, Cui-Zu Chang
abstract: The recent discovery of intrinsic superconductivity in stoichiometric FeTe films has renewed interest in the Te-rich end member of the iron chalcogenides for studies of unconventional and topological superconductivity, yet its intrinsic electronic structure remains unresolved. In this work, we combine molecular beam epitaxy, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), electrical transport measurements, density functional theory, and embedded dynamical mean-field theory to track the electronic reconstruction of 20-unit-cell FeTe films as Te annealing progressively removes excess interstitial Fe and drives the system from an antiferromagnetic metal to a superconductor. We find that this evolution is accompanied by recovered quasiparticle coherence, reduced electronic correlations, a Lifshitz transition, and a topological phase transition, yielding dxy-dominated hole and electron pockets that favor inter-pocket scattering. In addition, a shallow dxz/dyz-derived hole band located about 2 meV below the Fermi level may provide an incipient-band pairing channel, while scattering between the two electron pockets at M may offer additional pairing channels. High-resolution polarization-dependent laser ARPES measurements further reveal a topological surface state whose circular dichroism is consistent with the expected orbital-angular-momentum texture of stoichiometric FeTe. These results establish the intrinsic low-energy electronic structure of superconducting FeTe and identify the electronic states most relevant to superconductivity. The coexistence of intrinsic superconductivity and a topological surface state establishes stoichiometric FeTe as a promising platform for exploring topological superconductivity and possible Majorana bound states.
summary: This work investigates the electronic structure of FeTe as it transitions from an antiferromagnetic metal to a superconductor by annealing out excess iron. Using a combination of ARPES, transport measurements, and DFT/eDMFT, the authors map out the electronic reconstruction, identifying key topological features and orbital states that are crucial for the observed superconductivity.
main_problem: The study aims to understand the electronic reconstruction in FeTe as it transitions from an antiferromagnetic metal to a superconducting state, and to establish its intrinsic low-energy electronic structure.
main_result: The annealing process drives the system through a topological phase transition, revealing a low-energy structure featuring $d_{xy}$-dominated hole and electron pockets, and confirming the coexistence of intrinsic superconductivity and a topological surface state.
method: The research combines experimental techniques like ARPES and transport measurements with theoretical modeling using DFT and embedded Dynamical Mean-Field Theory (eDMFT).
model_or_system: The physical system is stoichiometric FeTe films, studied by monitoring the electronic structure evolution as excess interstitial Fe is removed via Te annealing, causing a transition from an AFM to a superconducting state.
key_observables: Quasiparticle coherence recovery, Lifshitz transition, topological phase transition, $d_{xy}$-dominated hole/electron pockets, and the circular dichroism signature of a topological surface state.
important_parameters: Superconducting critical temperatures ($T_c \approx 12-13 	ext{ K}$), magnetic ordering temperature ($T_N \approx 58 	ext{ K}$), and the energy level of a potential pairing band ($\approx 2 	ext{ meV}$ below $E_F$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed electronic changes are driven by the removal of excess interstitial Fe, leading to the intrinsic, stoichiometric electronic structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of Fermi surfaces and band structures across annealing stages, detailing the emergence of different orbital character pockets and the signature of the topological surface state via polarization-dependent ARPES.
paper_structure: The paper follows a progression from characterizing the initial state (AFM metal) to tracking the structural/chemical change (Te annealing) which drives the electronic evolution (Lifshitz/topological transitions) until the final superconducting, topologically non-trivial state is established.
why_interesting: The investigation into the interplay between electronic reconstruction, topological phases, and unconventional superconductivity in FeTe provides a rich platform for understanding correlated electron behavior beyond simple BCS models.
